prerequisites: Knowledge of drawing at Bachelor level is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with basic knowledge of computer-aided design techniques.
Develop the ability to see or imagine geometric shapes in space and mentally perform operations with them.
Enable students to understand tasks, synthesize ideas, and identify with technical language as a means of communication.
Acquire proficiency in handling drawing instruments and sketching parts as a means of quickly and precisely expressing graphic ideas.
Ensure students know and value standardization as a universal means of graphic language.
Capacity for spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Mechanical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing geometric constructions.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing representation systems to interpret and represent Engineering drawings.
Be able to know and apply representation standards and incorporate the use of technical terms in language.
Be able to know, understand and use computer-aided design programs to represent Engineering drawings.
Be able to understand, know and use graphic visualization techniques to improve spatial vision linked to engineering.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.5 x ETP1 + 0.1 x PA + 0.2 x PL + 0.2 x TIG, provided minimums are met. A minimum of 5 out of 10 is required for the final exam (ETP1) and the laboratory practices (PL). If the minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary calls, the final grade is 0.5 x ETP2 + 0.1 x PA + 0.2 x EPL + 0.2 x TIG, with a minimum of 5 out of 10 for the theoretical/practical exam (ETP2) and the laboratory practices exam (EPL).
